markets.rules_primary: If Zohran Mamdani leaves as Mayor of New York City before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
This market resolves based on when the departure is publicly announced or officially communicated, regardless of the effective date.

An acknowledgment that they will leave office due solely to the scheduled expiration of a constitutionally or legally mandated term limit does not satisfy the Payout Criterion. 

If the person leaves the role due to death (i.e., if the person dies while holding the role), all contracts on the person may resolve to the last fair price as determined in the sole discretion of the Exchange. Temporary leaves of absence, suspensions, or recusals do not constitute leaving, resigning from, or retiring from the role unless the individual formally and permanently ceases to hold the position. If the person vacates the role and then re-occupies the role, the contract may settle on the initial vacation of the role.

For "leave," cessation of holding the role qualifies, including resignation, retirement, removal, expulsion, expiration of term without renewal, recall, or other means by which the individual no longer occupies the role—this includes both voluntary and involuntary early departure AND the natural expiration of a term.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the event described in the Payout Criterion occurs.
markets.rules_primary: If the Republic of Ireland agrees to or announces a formal government decision to hold a national referendum in the Republic of Ireland on Irish reunification before Jan 1, 2030, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
An agreement or announcement qualifies if it involves any of the following:

Formal signing of treaties
Parliamentary approval with binding effect
Official ratification
Formal commitment by the head of state/government with constitutional authority
Official statements by authorized ministers
Official press releases
Formal declarations during government proceedings
Official statements to international bodies

Phased implementation announcements and multi-party agreements where the country is a signatory also qualify.

The following do NOT qualify:

Preliminary discussions
Conditional agreements contingent on circumstances
Opposition party statements
Leaked documents
Think-tank recommendations
General aspirations without specific commitment
Draft legislation without approval
Regional actions (unless specified)
Retraction of previously announced commitments

The referendum must be a national poll in the Republic of Ireland on Irish reunification. An unequivocal Government of Ireland decision to hold the poll, an official statement recording that decision, a constitutional referendum Bill passed by both Houses of the Oireachtas, or a ministerial polling-day order qualifies. A polling date is not required, and voting may occur after January 1, 2030. Party pledges, consultations, citizens' assemblies, preparatory legislation or research, and general statements of intent do not qualify. A Northern Ireland border-poll announcement alone does not qualify.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the event occurs.
markets.rules_primary: If legislation establishing universal health care has become law after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Universal health care means the law guarantees that every U.S. citizen and lawful permanent resident living in the 50 states or D.C. has health coverage. Coverage the law provides must include at least the essential health benefits defined in the Affordable Care Act, at no less than bronze-level actuarial value. People may instead keep other coverage that counts as minimum essential coverage under federal law, such as an employer plan, Medicare or Medicaid; the law qualifies if it automatically covers or enrolls each of those people who has no such coverage in coverage meeting that floor. A law that excludes other noncitizens or incarcerated people qualifies. Any program design qualifies, including single-payer. The guarantee counts when the law is enacted, even if coverage begins or phases in later or depends on rules an agency must still write. A law still counts if some people decline coverage or are not yet enrolled.

Apart from those exclusions, legislation that does not cover or automatically enroll all of those people does NOT count, such as one that only creates a public option or buy-in, lowers the Medicare eligibility age, expands Medicaid, extends ACA premium tax credits, or requires people to buy insurance. A right only to buy coverage does not count, even with subsidies. Coverage limited to particular diseases or services, a state law, or a federal law that only authorizes, funds or studies a future decision to create the guarantee does NOT count.
markets.title: Will legislation establishing universal health care become law before Jan 1, 2028?

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the event occurs.
markets.rules_primary: If the Senate passes legislation using a talking filibuster before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
For this market, a talking filibuster means either (1) the Senate passing a bill or joint resolution on a recorded vote with fewer than three-fifths of the Senators duly chosen and sworn voting yes, after one or more Senators held the floor in debate against it through a night, or throughout the sessions of two or more days with the Senate recessing in between, until they ran out of speeches under the two-speech limit of Rule XIX or gave up debating it, with no cloture, statute, rule, precedent or unanimous consent agreement capping the time for that debate other than Rule XIX, without cloture invoked on it after that debate began, and with the vote on passing it held, or set by an agreement reached, before the Senate next adjourned or recessed to a later day after they stopped, or (2) the Senate passing a bill or joint resolution on a recorded vote with fewer than three-fifths of the Senators duly chosen and sworn voting yes, after one or more Senators held the floor in debate against it, under a change to the rules or precedents of the Senate whose own terms let supporters of it force that vote without three-fifths of the Senators duly chosen and sworn once its opponents stop debating it.

Under (1) and (2), a conference report or motion to concur on it counts as it, and agreeing to one counts as passing it.
Under (1), the motion to proceed to it, a substitute amendment, and a bill with substantially the same text also count as it.
Under (2), a change that also lets fewer than three-fifths of Senators end debate while opponents are still debating does NOT count.
markets.title: Will the Senate pass legislation using a talking filibuster before Jan 1, 2027?

markets.rules_primary: If a bill increasing the number of Supreme Court seats above nine has become law after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2030, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The law must be signed by the President, become law without the President's signature, or become law through veto override. A bill that the President vetoes, including by pocket veto, without an override does NOT count.

A qualifying law increases the number of Justices of the Supreme Court above nine, the number set by 28 U.S.C. 1. The increase must take effect before Jan 1, 2030; the added seats need not be filled. Only Justices who hear the Court's appellate cases count, so a term-limits or staggered-appointment law qualifies only if it provides for more than nine Justices hearing the Court's appellate cases before Jan 1, 2030; Justices in senior status, or who hear only original-jurisdiction cases, do not count. A law that changes only the Court's jurisdiction, procedures, ethics rules or term limits, adds seats to lower courts, or proposes a constitutional amendment fixing the Court's size does NOT qualify. The law may be any vehicle, including a larger package whose enacted text contains a qualifying increase.

markets.rules_secondary:
The law must be signed by the President, become law without the President's signature, or become law through veto override. A bill that the President vetoes, including by pocket veto, without an override does NOT count.

A qualifying law raises the number of voting Representatives in the House above 435, the current number, whether directly, by a formula or schedule, or by admitting a State or giving the District of Columbia a voting Representative in addition to the 435. It counts when enacted, even if the added seats take effect, or are filled, after Jan 1, 2030. An increase that depends on a later vote, such as a statehood referendum, counts only if that vote approves it before Jan 1, 2030; later proclamations, elections and seating do not delay it. A law that changes only the number of non-voting Delegates or Resident Commissioners, creates a study commission, proposes a constitutional amendment, or changes how seats are apportioned while keeping 435 voting seats does NOT qualify. The law may be any vehicle, including a larger package whose enacted text contains a qualifying increase.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the event occurs.
markets.rules_primary: If the filibuster is abolished before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
For this market, the abolition of the filibuster means a change to the rules or precedents of the Senate under which debate on all bills and joint resolutions, and on motions to proceed to them, can be ended, over the objection of any Senator, by a simple majority, whether of the Senators voting or of the Senators duly chosen and sworn.

A change that lets fewer than three-fifths of Senators end debate only on some bills or joint resolutions (such as one named bill), or only once no Senator opposing a measure seeks recognition to debate it, does NOT count. Joint resolutions proposing amendments to the Constitution are disregarded.
Debate is ended only when the Senate can be brought to a vote on passing the bill or joint resolution, or on agreeing to the motion to proceed to it; tabling, recommitting or otherwise disposing of a measure without that vote does NOT count. A motion to proceed that the change makes non-debatable counts as one on which debate can be ended by a simple majority.
A standing order counts as a rule of the Senate however it is adopted; a unanimous consent agreement governing particular measures does NOT count.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if any component becomes impossible to occur (resolving to No) or all components have been satisfied (resolving to Yes).
markets.rules_primary: If ALL of the following occur: Party: Democratic, Unemployment rate: 4.0% or below, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
For all outcomes in this market, Party refers to the political party of the person inaugurated as President for the term beginning Jan 20, 2029, and Unemployment rate refers to the seasonally adjusted U.S. unemployment rate (U-3) for December 2029, as first published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics to one decimal place in its December 2029 Employment Situation report.

This is a combination market requiring ALL specified outcomes to occur for the contract to pay out. If ANY single component resolves to No or becomes impossible, the entire contract immediately resolves to No. Each component is resolved according to its corresponding Kalshi ruleset: Party (PRESPARTY), Unemployment rate (ECONSTATB). Later revisions will not affect the outcome. All stated bounds are inclusive. For example, “4.1% to 4.5%” includes both 4.1% and 4.5%, “5.1% or above” includes 5.1%, and “4.0% or below” includes 4.0%. In the case of a delay in data caused by a federal government shutdown impacting the reliability of the Source Agency, the market’s latest Expiration Date will be extended to the sooner of the release of the Underlying or six months after the end of the government shutdown, and a December 2029 Employment Situation report first published within that extension and before Sep 1, 2030 counts.

markets.rules_primary: If ALL of the following occur: Party: Democratic, Jobs added in 2029: Below 0, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
For all outcomes in this market, Party refers to the political party of the person inaugurated as President for the term beginning Jan 20, 2029, and Jobs added in 2029 refers to the change in seasonally adjusted total nonfarm payroll employment from December 2028 to December 2029, as first published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, normally in its December 2029 Employment Situation report. The change is the December 2029 level minus the December 2028 level in the seasonally adjusted Total nonfarm row of Table B-1 of the report that first publishes a December 2029 level. Later revisions, including the annual benchmark revision published with the January 2030 report, are excluded.

This is a combination market requiring ALL specified outcomes to occur for the contract to pay out. If ANY single component resolves to No or becomes impossible, the entire contract immediately resolves to No. Each component is resolved according to its corresponding Kalshi ruleset: Party (PRESPARTY), Jobs added in 2029 (PAYROLLS). Each band includes its lower bound and excludes its upper bound. For example, “0 to 500,000” includes 0 and excludes 500,000, “500,000 to 1 million” includes 500,000, and “1.5 million or above” includes 1.5 million. For the Jobs added in 2029 component, these bands apply in place of the PAYROLLS "between" range, which would include both endpoints, so a change exactly equal to a band's upper bound falls only in the next band. In the case of a delay in data caused by a federal government shutdown impacting the reliability of the Source Agency, the market’s latest Expiration Date will be extended to the sooner of the release of the Underlying or six months after the end of the government shutdown, and a December 2029 Employment Situation report first published within that extension and before Sep 1, 2030 counts.

Address the matter described by the specified judgment
Be issued through a written order, opinion, judgment, or decision

The June 23, 2025 order denying Visa's motion to dismiss, or any later ruling on a motion to dismiss
A consent decree, settlement, or voluntary dismissal, including a consent decree entered by the court
A ruling in any other Visa antitrust matter, including the payment card interchange fee litigation
Oral rulings from the bench unless reduced to a written order
Tentative rulings that are not made final
Administrative or scheduling orders

markets.rules_primary: If the U.S. government has taken operational control of any private AI company or project before Jan 1, 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The following qualify as takeovers that trigger the Payout Criterion:
The President of the United States, Congress, or any federal agency has announced or enacted legislation, executive order, or regulatory action that would result in the United States government acquiring 50% or more ownership stake in any private AI company or project
The United States government has actually acquired 50% or more ownership stake in any private AI company or project through any mechanism including but not limited to: purchase, eminent domain, legislative action, or court order
The United States government has taken operational control of any private AI company or project through conservatorship, receivership, or similar legal mechanism where the government directs strategic or executive decision-making regardless of equity ownership percentage
A legally binding court order or executive action placing these AI operations under federal or agencies' active management
A bill has become federal law specifically authorizing or mandating the nationalization or takeover of any private AI company or project, regardless of whether the acquisition has yet occurred
The President issues an executive order specifically directing the acquisition, nationalization, or federal operational takeover of any private AI company or project

The following do NOT satisfy the Payout Criterion:
Government contracts or purchases from any private AI company or project
Regulatory actions that do not transfer ownership or control
Antitrust breakups that do not result in government ownership
Bankruptcy proceedings unless resulting in government ownership/control
Government equity stakes below 50% unless accompanied by operational control
State or local government actions (only federal actions qualify)
Conditional announcements dependent on future events
Proposed legislation that has not been enacted

If the government assumes control due to an emergency (e.g., wartime powers, executive seizure), the market resolves to Yes only if such control is accompanied by language indicating ongoing federal management or ownership. Control of a single AI project within a company resolves to Yes if the government gains enforceable management over that project, and the project is independently identifiable and material (e.g., a standalone system or training pipeline, not just a subfeature).
markets.title: Will the US government take control of any AI company or project before 2028?

Caretaker or interim governments appointed temporarily before formal government formation do not count for determining party status.

A sole 'minority' government designation (e.g. 'Party X minority') means the relevant party is the ruling government but does not have a confidence and supply agreement with any party or a majority of seats in the parliament (or equivalent legislature). markets.rules_primary: If CK Hutchison has achieved the superior outcome in the trial-level resolution of its Panama ports arbitration (originally filed in the ICC), then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The Panama ports arbitration is the International Chamber of Commerce arbitration brought against the Republic of Panama over the Balboa and Cristobal terminals by Panama Ports Company, CK Hutchison's subsidiary. A recovery by Panama Ports Company is a recovery by CK Hutchison for the purposes of this market. CK Hutchison's separate treaty-based claim against Panama, and its arbitration against Maersk, do not resolve this market. If no trial-level resolution occurs before the expiration date, the market resolves to No.

CK Hutchison achieves the superior outcome through the following exclusive hierarchy:

Net Monetary Recovery (Highest Priority): CK Hutchison achieves the superior outcome if they receive a larger net monetary award than all opposing parties combined (after offsetting any awards against CK Hutchison). Attorney's fees and costs are excluded.

Substantive Legal Victory (Second Priority): If no net monetary advantage exists, CK Hutchison achieves the superior outcome if they prevail on claims seeking the largest dollar amount of relief in their original pleadings, or if relief amounts are equal, on the greater number of primary causes of action.

Case Termination Advantage (Third Priority): If the case terminates without substantive judgment, CK Hutchison achieves the superior outcome if (as defendant) all claims are dismissed with prejudice, or (as plaintiff) opposing parties voluntarily dismiss all claims with prejudice. All other termination scenarios result in no superior outcome for any party.

Settlements: If parties settle with a disclosed net payment to CK Hutchison, CK Hutchison achieves the superior outcome. If parties settle with a disclosed net payment from CK Hutchison to opposing parties, CK Hutchison does not achieve the superior outcome. If parties settle with mutual releases and no disclosed payment direction, or if settlement terms are sealed and no Source Agency reports payment direction within 7 days of settlement announcement, no party achieves a superior outcome.

Key exclusions: Applies only to trial-level resolution and specifically excludes all appeals processes. Procedural victories alone do not constitute superior outcomes.
markets.title: Will CK Hutchison win its Panama ports arbitration?

markets.rules_primary: If states that have enacted the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact possess at least 270 electoral votes before Jan 1, 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
For purposes of this Contract, a state or jurisdiction has "enacted" NPVIC legislation when such legislation has been signed into law by the governor, has become law without the governor's signature after the constitutional waiting period, or has been enacted by veto override; or has otherwise become law. The effective date of the law is not relevant; only that it has been enacted.

Electoral votes are counted based on the apportionment in effect at the time of when the relevant law is enacted. States that have withdrawn from the compact through repeal legislation are not counted toward the total.

If a state's membership in the compact is invalidated by a final court ruling before Jan 1, 2028, that state's electoral votes are not counted.
Conditional adoptions (e.g., Nevada's requirement for voter approval) are not counted until all conditions are satisfied.

Examples that WOULD resolve the market to Yes:

270 or more electoral votes worth of states have enacted NPVIC legislation before Jan 1, 2028
States totaling 269 electoral votes have joined, and one additional state with at least 1 electoral vote enacts NPVIC legislation before Jan 1, 2028

Examples that would NOT resolve the market to Yes:

States totaling 269 electoral votes have enacted NPVIC legislation by Jan 1, 2028
States totaling 270 electoral votes have passed NPVIC legislation in both chambers but governors have not yet signed
markets.title: Will the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact reach 270 electoral votes before 2028?

markets.rules_secondary:
For purposes of this Contract, a state or jurisdiction has "enacted" NPVIC legislation when such legislation has been signed into law by the governor, has become law without the governor's signature after the constitutional waiting period, or has been enacted by veto override; or has otherwise become law. The effective date of the law is not relevant; only that it has been enacted.

Electoral votes are counted based on the apportionment in effect at the time of when the relevant law is enacted. States that have withdrawn from the compact through repeal legislation are not counted toward the total.

If a state's membership in the compact is invalidated by a final court ruling before Jan 1, 2034, that state's electoral votes are not counted.
Conditional adoptions (e.g., Nevada's requirement for voter approval) are not counted until all conditions are satisfied.

Examples that WOULD resolve the market to Yes:

270 or more electoral votes worth of states have enacted NPVIC legislation before Jan 1, 2034
States totaling 269 electoral votes have joined, and one additional state with at least 1 electoral vote enacts NPVIC legislation before Jan 1, 2034

Examples that would NOT resolve the market to Yes:

States totaling 269 electoral votes have enacted NPVIC legislation by Jan 1, 2034
States totaling 270 electoral votes have passed NPVIC legislation in both chambers but governors have not yet signed

markets.rules_secondary: Change as of 5:00 AM ET December 15 2023: The market's terms and conditions note that, "The Expiration Date of the Contract shall be the sooner of the date of the first 10:00 AM ET following the occurrence of an event that is encompassed in the Payout Criterion or the first 10:00 AM ET after date." However, the Payout Criterion only encompasses Amazon being found liable for the counts alleged by the FTC, and not just a decision or settlement happening. The language will be amended such that expiration, like the last trading date, will happen once claims are settled, regardless of whether Amazon is found liable for the counts alleged. This will be done as part of the CFTC's provisions that allow for non-economic changes to contracts, and will be reflected in the rules today, December 15th.

"New single-player story content" means narrative content for Grand Theft Auto VI that was not available in the game at its initial release (its first commercial release on any platform, including pre-order, special-edition, and day-one update content) and that adds new story missions, chapters, episodes, or a story campaign playable in the game's single-player mode (Story Mode), whether free or paid, and whether delivered as a title update, a downloadable expansion, or a standalone expansion that Rockstar Games designates as content for Grand Theft Auto VI. It has to be for the non-online, single-player Story Mode. GTA Online DLC would not qualify, even if it adds narrative missions or can be played solo.

Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the companies Rockstar Games and Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if any component becomes impossible to occur (resolving to No) or all components have been satisfied (resolving to Yes).
markets.rules_primary: If ALL of the following occur: Party: Democratic, S&P 500 change: Below -10%, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
For all outcomes in this market, Party refers to the political party of the person inaugurated as President for the term beginning Jan 20, 2029, and S&P 500 change refers to the percent change in the S&P 500 index from its closing value on Jan 19, 2029 to its closing value on Dec 31, 2029.

This is a combination market requiring ALL specified outcomes to occur for the contract to pay out. If ANY single component resolves to No or becomes impossible, the entire contract immediately resolves to No. Each component is resolved according to its corresponding Kalshi ruleset: Party (PRESPARTY), S&P 500 change (INX). Revisions published after expiration will not be considered. The percent change is not rounded. Each band includes its lower bound and excludes its upper bound. For example, “0% to 10%” includes 0% and excludes 10%, “10% to 20%” includes 10%, and “20% or above” includes 20%. For the S&P 500 change component, these bands apply in place of the INX "between" range, which would include both endpoints, so a change exactly equal to a band's upper bound falls only in the next band.
markets.title: Will a Democrat win in 2028 AND the 2029 S&P 500 change be below -10%?

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the law is enacted
markets.rules_primary: If a constitutional reform reducing the number of proportional-representation (plurinominal) seats in the Chamber of Deputies or the Senate is enacted in Mexico before Jan 1, 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Enactment requires completion of all constitutional and legal requirements for the legislation to become binding law. For a constitutional amendment, that means passage with the required supermajorities and completion of the ratification process.

The reform counts only once its decree is published in the Diario Oficial de la Federación, even if the seat reduction takes effect later. Each market's deadline is 12:00 AM Mexico City time on its date. A decree counts by the date of the Diario Oficial de la Federación edition that publishes it, so one in an edition dated on or after a market's date does not count for that market, even if that edition is posted online the evening before. Only the federal Chamber of Deputies and Senate count, and the reduction is measured in the number of proportional-representation seats. A reform that changes how proportional-representation seats are filled without reducing their number does NOT count.
markets.title: Will Mexico pass a reform cutting plurinominal seats before Jan 1, 2028?
